cards.explanation: The answer is Manasseh. The text says, "So Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, received their inheritance." (Joshua 16:4) Two sons of Joseph, one inheritance. That's a lot of names to keep straight, friends.

The answer is that they do not drive them out. The text says, "But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer." (Joshua 16:10) Gezer was part of the border Ephraim received, and the Canaanites stayed living there among the Ephraimites. Some jobs get left half-done. I once left a whole batch of dough on the counter overnight and called it resting.

The answer is True. The text says, "So the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites to this day, but they are forced laborers." (Joshua 16:10) They stayed in Gezer, and they worked as forced laborers. Pay attention to that word "but," friends. It's doing a lot of work in that verse.

The answer is because he was a man of war. The text says Machir "…had received Gilead and Bashan because Machir was a man of war." (Joshua 17:1) Machir was Manasseh's firstborn and the father of the Gileadites. The text gives the reason in one short phrase, no extra paperwork.

The answer is Eleazar the priest, Joshua and the leaders. The text says, "They approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders…" (Joshua 17:4) Five daughters walked up to the priest, Israel's leader and the leaders, and they brought their case right to the top. I'd have been hiding behind the cookie jar, but they walked right up.

The answer is Moses. The daughters say, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." (Joshua 17:4) They don't just ask. They point to what the LORD already commanded. Five daughters, one command, and they walked in carrying it like a recipe they knew by heart.

The answer is False. The text says, "So Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers, in keeping with the command of the LORD." (Joshua 17:4) Nobody got sent home, friends. They received land among their father's brothers.

The answer is the rest of the sons of Manasseh. The text says, "…the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh." (Joshua 17:6) The daughters got their inheritance among Manasseh's sons, and Gilead stayed with the rest of those sons. Think of Gilead as the big batch set out beyond the Jordan, a separate tray from the ten shares in verse 5. Keep your eyes on the trays, bakers, and you're golden.

The answer is no, because the Canaanites are determined to stay. The text says the descendants of Manasseh "…were unable to occupy these cities, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in this land." (Joshua 17:12) The cities were assigned to Manasseh, but the Canaanites weren't packing. It's like holding the deed to a house while somebody sits in the living room.

The answer is False. The text says that when the Israelites grew stronger, "…they put the Canaanites to forced labor; but they failed to drive them out completely." (Joshua 17:13) Stronger, yes. Finished, no. Pay attention to that "but," friends.

The answer is why they got only one portion. The sons of Joseph ask Joshua, "Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance?" (Joshua 17:14) They bring up the size of their family and say the LORD has blessed them. Joshua, Israel's leader, is the one on the receiving end of that question.

The answer is blessed. The sons of Joseph say, "We have many people, because the LORD has blessed us abundantly." (Joshua 17:14) They credit the LORD for their big numbers. A crowded house is a good problem to have, friends.

The answer is to go clear land in the forest. Joshua answers, "If you have so many people that the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you, go to the forest and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim." (Joshua 17:15) The Perizzites and the Rephaim are peoples whose land is out there. So Joshua's answer is to go and clear the forest.

The answer is chariots. The sons of Joseph say, "…all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, both in Beth-shean with its towns and in the Valley of Jezreel." (Joshua 17:16) They say it right after telling Joshua the hill country is not enough for them. I think they were feeling the size of the challenge. I know that feeling. It's me staring at a triple batch.

The answer is True. Joshua says to the house of Joseph, "You have many people and great strength. You shall not have just one allotment…" (Joshua 17:17) He had heard the complaint and he answers it. They're getting more than one.

The answer is that they can drive them out. Joshua says, "Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out." (Joshua 17:18) He names the chariots and the strength right out loud, and he still says they can drive them out. Iron chariots on one side, and Joshua's word on the other.
